why: The lesson teaches saying how you are with estoy; this example is the question (taught in meeting-people-3) and doesn't show estoy.
Uses soy instead of me llamo, which the notice never explains; meanwhile ¿cómo te llamas?, which the notice teaches and practice 3 tests, has no example.

text.en: How long have you been here?

why: This ask is word for word the answer to practice 3, so the learner hears that answer before being asked for it.

fix.en: Are you new in the neighborhood?

ask.said: La señora de la tienda habla rápido. ¿Qué pides?
ask.en: The lady at the store talks fast. What do you ask?

why: Re-teaches getting-by-1 (asking someone to repeat) instead of practising ¿me puede…? for a new request.

ask.said: Tienes muchas bolsas y no puedes abrir la puerta. ¿Qué pides?
ask.en: You've got lots of bags and can't open the door. What do you ask?

answer.said: ¿Me puede abrir la puerta, por favor?
answer.en: Could you open the door for me, please?

text.goal: Ask the ticket clerk to speak more slowly.

why: Same task as getting-by-1's mission (ask for slower speech); the mission should use ¿me puede…? for a request of its own.

fix.goal: Ask the ticket clerk to help you.

text.en: Hi! What can I get you?

why: The point is ordering with me da; this example is the server's question and doesn't show me da.

fix.said: Me da un pan dulce, por favor.
fix.en: Can I have a pan dulce, please?

ask.en: How do you want your tacos?

why: The answer repeats example 1 (¿Con todo?) with por favor added.

ask.en: Do you want salsa on your torta?

text.en: What are you looking for at the pharmacy?

why: The lesson is about answering ¿qué buscaba?, but this ask uses the plain present buscas, so the learner never practises hearing the staff's form.

fix.en: Good afternoon, what are you looking for?

ask.said: Solo quieres mirar en la tienda. ¿Qué dices?
ask.en: You just want to browse in the store. What do you say?

why: The answer repeats example 4 (Nada más estoy viendo, gracias) with one word swapped.

answer.said: Solo estoy viendo la fruta, gracias.
answer.en: Just looking at the fruit, thanks.

text.en: What do you need at the market today?

why: Uses the present necesitas instead of the staff's ¿qué necesitaba?, which is what the lesson teaches you to answer.

fix.en: Good morning, what do you need today?

ask.said: Una torta cuesta cincuenta pesos. ¿Cuánto cuestan dos?
ask.en: One torta is fifty pesos. How much are two?

why: The ask contains the answer's form (cuestan), and it tests arithmetic and totals, the next lesson's point, rather than asking a price.

ask.said: Te gusta un sombrero en el mercado. ¿Qué preguntas?
ask.en: You like a hat at the market. What do you ask?
